recentItems.title: CBS / WLYH-TV 15 Commercial Breaks (March 21st, 1989)
recentItems.description:
Join Broadcast Plaza on Discord today!
https://discord.gg/MCS46peRyz

Commercial breaks from a CBS Tuesday Movie airing of the 1984 movie "Purple Hearts". Aired on Tuesday, March, 21st, 1989. Recorded from now-former CBS affiliate WLYH-TV 15 in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, at the time owned by Gateway Communications.

Sourced from a tape from a family member's former collection.

WLYH served as one of multiple CBS affiliates in the Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA market from 1963 until 1995, when Harrisburg CBS affiliate WHP-TV 21 took over the station's operations via LMA. After affiliations with UPN and The CW, at the start of 2016, the station's non-license assets were moved to a new WHP subchannel, as channel 15 was sold off to Sinclair Broadcast Group political commentator Armstrong Williams' television company, Howard Stirk Holdings. Today, channel 15 operates as WXBU, and now serves as an affiliate of the Spanish-language network Univision.

recentItems.title: WTAJ News This Morning | Jordan Tracy’s Last Day – Highlights (6/7/24)
recentItems.description:
Join Broadcast Plaza on Discord today!
https://discord.gg/MCS46peRyz

After nearly 8 years at the station, today was the last day for WTAJ’s Jordan Tracy. He is transferring to co-owned KTVX in Salt Lake City, Utah.

Jordan Tracy held a large variety of roles at the station, including reporter, producer, political reporter, sports anchor and High School football show host, host of lifestyle show Studio 814, and for the last 3 years, anchor of WTAJ’s morning and noon newscasts. He had become a staple of the station and one of their longest-tenured on air talent in recent history.

This is an edited look at his final morning show. Multiple segments looking back at his time at the station and farewell messages from past and present talent and local community members were included within the two hour newscast, starting mainly in the second half hour.

Newscast anchored by Jordan Tracy and Alyssa Royster, with meteorologist Kaitlyn Sheehan.

Recorded over the air from WTAJ-TV, virtual channel 10.1 (RF channel 24)

5PM generic news open on WJAC-TV, the Sinclair Broadcast Group owned NBC affiliate in Johnstown, Pennsylvania.

During today's morning news, WJAC made a voiceover artist change, switching from Scott Chapin to John Beach. Scott Chapin had been the main voice of the station since some point in the mid-2000's, however at the end of 2023, Chapin officially retired from full-time voiceover work. John Beach has gained more widespread used in recent years, including on sister station WHP-TV to the east in Harrisburg. Some Scott Chapin recordings are still used for now, including newscast reopens, weather opens, and sponsor bumps. It is expected those will be slowly replaced in the coming weeks. The station also uses Brian Lee for many promos.

The typical Sinclair group-wide news graphics, and "Sinclair: Curves & Glass" by Warner Chappell Production Music, have both been retained.

Jen Johnson anchors.

recentItems.title: WTAJ News Opens (October 2023)
recentItems.description:
Join Broadcast Plaza on Discord today!
https://discord.gg/MCS46peRyz

Here is a full montage of opens for newscasts and some select other station-produced programming on WTAJ-TV, recorded over the last week and a half.

As previously seen on this channel, WTAJ debuted a new set, new graphics, and new music at 4pm on Wednesday, October 18th.

The new set replaces the set first debuted in February 2013 as the station began broadcasting news in HD. I was never a fan of the set. The set prominently featued their former graphics they used from 2013-2017 in the background, and once those graphics were changed out for Nexstar's CBS graphics, it just became a clashing eyesore imo. This new set is comparable to other recent Nexstar set debuts like in-state sister stations WJET/WFXP in Erie (Main difference being it looks like WTAJ had less space to work with) It is the best set in the market, but this market has low set standards to begin with (WJAC's debuted way back in 2008 (modified in 2011 though) and is also behind the times, and WATM/WWCP are in a tiny secondary studio that is rather bare bones)

Graphics-wise, the station switches from one Nexstar graphics look to another, with CBS-1 being dropped in favor of MOD-1, a flatter look that first debuted in 2019 on KOIN 6 in Portland, Oregon. Personally, I prefer the look and aesthetic of CBS-1. It honestly still looks cleaner and nicer than some other Rey Rodriguez-designed looks debuted as recently as this year (Looking at you, WFMZ.) However, WTAJ uses MOD-1 a lot better than how they used CBS-1. With the former look, they didn't use a lot of the provided transitions most of the time and rather just used fades, which cheapened the look. They use all the proper transitions with MOD-1 which is an improvement.

For music, the station drops one Stephen Arnold Music package for another, switching from "Convergence" to "Aerial". WTAJ was one of the last stations to use Convergence, which originally was made for WVEC in Hampton, Virginia. This is probably an unpopular opinion considering the opinion's I see from a lot of this community, but I personally think Aerial is better here than Convergence in this case. With all due respect, Convergence today sounds kinda dated in my view. It was originally created 22 years ago in 2001 and does not sound that modern. Aerial is a newer package and is also much more expansive with it's selection of cuts. I have one gripe with Aerial being used here. That issue is that it's already used in this market at Penn State University's Centre County Report. Granted, WTAJ uses a larger variety of cuts than PSU uses. I think there were some better music choices out there. However I still think it's an improvement over Convergence.

Eric Gordon remains here as voiceover. He replaced Paul Turner in that role at the end of 2018.

recentItems.title: WTAJ News at 4 Open [NEW SET/GRAPHICS/MUSIC] (10/18/23)
recentItems.description:
Join Broadcast Plaza on Discord today!
https://discord.gg/MCS46peRyz

4pm news open from WTAJ-TV, the Nexstar owned CBS affiliate licensed to Altoona, Pennsylvania, and also serving Johnstown and State College.

After 10 years of their former news set and music, and 6 years of their former graphics, WTAJ has debuted a brand new set, new graphics, and new music today at 4pm.

The former CBS-1 graphics in use since Fall 2017 have been replaced with MOD-1, a slightly newer look created by Nexstar's internal graphics hub based at WKRN in Nashville. The music was changed from one Stephen Arnold Music package from another, switching from Convergence to Aerial. Eric Gordon remains as station voiceover, a role he has held since late 2018 or early 2019.

Anchored by Maggie Smolka and Marty Radovanic, with Meteorologist Christopher Nallan

More WTAJ content will be posted in the coming days.

Recorded Over The Air from WTAJ (RF channel 24, Virtual channel 10.1)
